title: Ash-Shakur, the Appreciative
hook: the Appreciative, who rewards the smallest good

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Wadud, the Loving, whose love is shown. Your line was loved.

You held a door. You wiped the counter someone else left sticky. You moved the scooter off the sidewalk so the next person with a stroller wouldn't have to. Nobody saw. Nobody said thanks. Easy to file under: didn't count. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told of a man walking down a road who found a thorny branch lying across it. He moved it out of the way, so it wouldn't hurt anyone. That's the whole deed. And the hadith, in Sahih al-Bukhari, says God thanked him for it, and forgave him. God thanked him. For a branch. Today: Ash-Shakur.
screen: `NOBODY SAW.` → `A THORNY BRANCH ON THE ROAD.` → `GOD THANKED HIM.`

segments.voice: Ash-Shakur comes from shukr, the word for thanks from the very start of the path. A person with shukr is grateful. But God doesn't need anything from us, so what does it mean for him to be shakur? Scholars explain it as appreciation: he notices the smallest good and rewards it far beyond its size. A branch moved, a whole life forgiven. That's the scale. The Qur'an puts it in two short lines near its end. In Pickthall's translation: "And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then." In the Arabic it's a dharrah, a speck, some say the tiniest ant. Nothing is too small to be seen, and answered. And the Prophet backed it up in a hadith in Sahih Muslim: don't look down on any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face. A smile is on the list. Now look back at this week, because every name has pointed here. Al-Fattah opened. Al-'Alim knew what the heart hides. As-Sami' heard the woman in Medina. Al-Latif worked too finely to see. Al-Halim held back. Al-Wadud loved, and showed it. And Ash-Shakur notices the smallest thing you did, and doesn't let it disappear. Seven days, eight names, one picture running through them: in the Qur'an's telling, nothing a person does is too small, too quiet, or too hidden to count.
screen: `SHUKR — THANKS, FROM GOD.` · `AN ATOM'S WEIGHT OF GOOD.` · `EVEN A CHEERFUL FACE.` · `EIGHT NAMES THIS WEEK.` · then, large: `NOTHING SMALL IS LOST.`

segments.voice: Go back over today and find the smallest kind thing anyone did for you: the barista who remembered your name, the coworker who refilled the printer, the kid who put their plate in the sink without being asked. Choose one, and picture thanking them, naming the small thing so they know it was seen. If you pray, you can thank God for it too.
Ash-Shakur. The Appreciative: the One who notices the smallest good and rewards it far beyond its size. Today's word.
Your line: nothing small is lost. Not even a branch moved off a road. Day two hundred fifty-two, and a week of names, done.

howItsDone: Many Muslims take the hadith of the thorny branch literally and clear obstacles from paths and roads, and the Prophet counted removing harm from the road as a branch of faith.

original.note: Arabic: the Appreciative. from shukr, thanks: here, the One who rewards small good richly.

trapdoor: what you thought: we're supposed to thank God.
what it means: God is the Appreciative one, who notices the smallest good and rewards it far beyond its size.
what a scholar hears: the hadith uses the verb shakara of God: he thanked the man. scholars read God's shukr as reward, never as need.
